quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Motorcycles must have passenger footrests. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off the bike.

questions.question: How can you get sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will make you sober. Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing can speed this up.

questions.question: Before riding, check the throttle. When you release it, the throttle should:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply steady pressure to both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: It can be hard to ride right after rain starts because:

options.text: Some drivers may not react quickly to the rain
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather

questions.explanation: When rain just starts, the road is especially slippery. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, mixing with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: If you must ride on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes together.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Has little effect on whether other drivers can see you
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you
questions.explanation: Proper lane position helps you see better and be seen better. Good positioning also helps you avoid wind from other vehicles.

questions.question: You approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes and give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane to see around vehicles ahead
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you to use their headlights
Ride slower to have more time to avoid hazards

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower to have more time to avoid hazards
questions.explanation: At night, ride at a lower speed than during the day. This gives you a better chance to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Can drinking one alcoholic drink before riding affect you?

options.text: No, it will not lead to a DUI conviction.
No, it will never affect your riding skills.
Yes, it can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Your ability to ride safely can be affected after just one drink. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What is the most important way to get the most protection from your helmet?
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: What should you do if a tailgater is following you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make the danger worse because they may keep tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get across the surface faster.
Make the zigzag motion bigger to alert other drivers.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over grooves or gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight. Trying to zigzag to fight the weave keeps you from staying in your lane and is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Avoid sudden movements if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements if you can.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
No, motorcycles are smaller so they do not have blind spots.
Mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will only make them keep tailgating, just at a higher speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How often should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle for safety before you ride. A small problem on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than a small problem on a car.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should you do with your mirrors?

options.text: Only the lead rider should check them.
Do not check them often because they distract you.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when riding in a group. This helps you see the riders behind you and keeps track of the group.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when you start the engine?
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. A neutral light on the dashboard will turn on when the motorcycle is in neutral and the ignition is on.

questions.question: What should NOT be included in a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint inspection is not necessary.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping your motorcycle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. End in first gear so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: If hazards are on your right, which side of the lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane.
